en: The One Hundred and Eight Names of Mañjuśrī: A Sanskrit Hymn Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heavens, Imperial Censor, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master of the Transmission of the Teaching, the Subject Dharma Heaven, by Imperial Decree.
I now proclaim the one hundred and eight names of Mañjuśrī, whose supreme qualities are most excellent.

By receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting them three times each day, whatever aspirations one seeks will certainly manifest; one should maintain the practice according to the ritual instructions.
The body is perpetually pure, and karmic obstructions are eliminated.
Even when entering battle or amidst various fears, Mañjuśrī manifests his form to provide protection.
If one constantly recites and contemplates this, one will swiftly realize Bodhi.
